h.strategy: Use retrieved findings to classify settings as strong, weak, neutral or harmful, and to identify which settings can disconnect other parts from the outcome. Propose hypotheses only of two kinds. Self-conditioning: the edit's effect depends on the value it replaces, being more negative when that value is strong and more positive when it is empty or harmful. Disconnection: when the edited part cannot influence the outcome, its effect shrinks toward zero, so the direction is lower if the edit usually helps and higher if it usually hurts. Directions refer to the signed effect. For each hypothesis, state the edit's usual sign and a one-sentence mechanism. Cover varied edit fields and values. The critic should replace any hypothesis with an uncertain usual sign, competing effects or reliance on partial redundancy.

hyps.why: Replacing a weak parameter-free pool on the final deep-path edge with a conv gains more than replacing the average op, which includes conv1x1 and conv3x3 itself.
With edge 0 removed node 1 outputs zeros, so the usually positive conv on edge 1->2 has nothing to process and its gain collapses toward zero.
Node 1 is dead when edge 0 is none, so upgrading edge 1->3 cannot influence the output and its usual positive effect vanishes.
With edge 2->3 removed node 2 never reaches the output, so upgrading its input edge from node 0 is inert.
The usually harmful pool on edge 1->2 becomes irrelevant when node 2 is disconnected from the output, so its negative effect rises toward zero.
Deleting edge 0 also silences edges 2 and 4, and losing a strong conv there costs more than losing a skip or pool.
Replacing a strong parametric edge into the output node with a pool discards more capacity than replacing weaker ops.
Removing a strong parametric direct input to node 2 hurts more than removing a skip or pool.
Without the direct 0->3 edge, cutting edge 2->3 removes one of only two remaining routes to the output, so the loss is much larger than when the direct edge provides redundancy.
When node 1 is dead the output relies only on edge 3 and the 0->2->3 path, so removing the direct edge costs far more than when edge 3 is partly redundant.
